rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for trouble or inconvenience, including saying that something is no bother.

example.english: This matter is really a bother.
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 si6 zan1 hai6 hou2 maa4 faan4

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb when bother means annoy or disturb someone.

example.english: You bother me all the time, and I'm about to lose it.
example.traditional: 你成日煩住我，我就嚟頂唔順喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 sing4 jat6 faan4 zyu6 ngo5 ngo5 zau6 lai4 ding2 m4 seon6 laa3

rows.note: Use this for an actual commotion or disturbance rather than ordinary inconvenience.

example.english: People started fighting downstairs, and the whole street was in a bother.
example.traditional: 樓下有人打交，成條街都騷動起嚟。
example.jyutping: lau4 haa6 jau5 jan4 daa2 gaau1 seng4 tiu4 gaai1 dou1 sou1 dung6 hei2 lei4

rows.note: Use this when bother means care about or pay attention to something, not when someone is annoying.

example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 lei5 di1 haan4 jin4 haan4 jyu5

rows.note: Use this for the positive take-the-trouble-to-do sense, especially when someone makes an effort.

example.english: Thanks for going to the bother of arranging a surprise for me.
example.traditional: 真係多謝你咁費心幫我安排個驚喜。
example.jyutping: zan1 hai6 do1 ze6 nei5 gam3 fai3 sam1 bong1 ngo5 on1 paai4 go3 ging1 hei2

rows.note: Use this colloquial negative construction for not bothering to do V or avoiding the trouble.

example.english: I won't bother arguing with him; I'd rather go to bed early.
example.traditional: 我唔會費事同佢拗，早啲瞓好過。
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 wui5 fai3 si6 tung4 keoi5 aau3 zou2 di1 fan3 hou2 gwo3
